title: Dual inhibition of KDM4B and KDM5A disassembles the PAX3-FOXO1 transcriptional program in fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
authors: Yuan, Junhong; Han, Qilei; Ren, Pengxuan; Bai, Fang; Zhang, Xianglei; Li, Kai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究KDM4B/KDM5A抑制剂对PAX3-FOXO1转录程序的调控，虽涉及转录因子但无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅用深度学习做药物筛选，与本课题核心关联弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma (FP-RMS) is driven by the oncogenic transcription factor PAX3-FOXO1 and is associated with poor clinical outcome. The histone demethylase KDM4B has been implicated in sustaining PAX3-FOXO1-dependent transcriptional programs, but the epigenetic regulatory mechanisms supporting this network remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We employed a deep learning-based drug discovery strategy and identified a novel small-molecule, Compound 01. Functional and mechanistic analyses were then performed to delineate cooperative interactions among KDM4B, KDM5A, and PAX3-FOXO1, and to evaluate the impact of pharmacological perturbation on the stability of this transcriptional network in FP-RMS models. RESULTS: In this study, we identified Compound 01 with dual activity against KDM4B and KDM5A that triggers proteasome-dependent loss of both proteins. Mechanistically, we uncover a reciprocal stabilization loop in which KDM4B, KDM5A, and PAX3-FOXO1 reinforce each other to sustain the PAX3-FOXO1 transcriptional state. Pharmacological disruption of this axis by Compound 01 collapses the PAX3-FOXO1-driven oncogenic transcriptional program, suppresses key downstream targets, and markedly impairs FP-RMS cell proliferation and metastatic potential. CONCLUSION: These findings identify KDM5A as a critical epigenetic partner of the PAX3-FOXO1 network and establish dual KDM4B/KDM5A targeting as a strategy to destabilize PAX3-FOXO1 transcriptional circuitry in FP-RMS.
abstract_zh: 背景：融合阳性横纹肌肉瘤（FP-RMS）由致癌转录因子PAX3-FOXO1驱动，并与不良临床结局相关。组蛋白去甲基化酶KDM4B被认为在维持PAX3-FOXO1依赖性转录程序中发挥作用，但支持该网络的表观遗传调控机制尚未完全阐明。方法：我们采用基于深度学习的药物发现策略，鉴定出一种新型小分子化合物Compound 01。随后进行了功能和机制分析，以描绘KDM4B、KDM5A和PAX3-FOXO1之间的协同相互作用，并评估药理学干预对FP-RMS模型中该转录网络稳定性的影响。结果：在本研究中，我们鉴定出Compound 01具有针对KDM4B和KDM5A的双重活性，可触发蛋白酶体依赖性的两种蛋白降解。机制上，我们揭示了一个相互稳定环路，其中KDM4B、KDM5A和PAX3-FOXO1相互增强，以维持PAX3-FOXO1转录状态。通过Compound 01对该轴的药理学破坏，使PAX3-FOXO1驱动的致癌转录程序崩溃，抑制关键下游靶标，并显著损害FP-RMS细胞增殖和转移潜力。结论：这些发现将KDM5A确定为PAX3-FOXO1网络的关键表观遗传伙伴，并确立双重靶向KDM4B/KDM5A作为在FP-RMS中破坏PAX3-FOXO1转录回路的一种策略。
